Explanation.Title: Explanation
Explanation.Intro1: Lunare follows the traditional lunar count used to measure time by observing the Moon’s phases.
Explanation.Intro2: Before modern calendars, days were counted starting from the new moon and following its natural cycle of about 29–30 days.
Explanation.LunarDayText1: The lunar day shows how many days have passed since the beginning of the Moon’s cycle.
Explanation.LunarDayText2: Day 1 is the new moon, day 14 is the full moon, and from day 15 the Moon wanes until day 30.
Explanation.EpactText1: The epact shows how many lunar days had already passed at the beginning of the year.
Explanation.EpactText2: It is used as the starting point for the lunar count.
Explanation.CountText1: To find the lunar day, three values are added: the epact, the months passed since March and the day of the month.
Explanation.CountText2: If the result is greater than 30, 30 is subtracted until the value fits the lunar cycle.
Explanation.ExampleCalc:
Example:
Epact 29
Months since March: 11
Day of month: 11

29 + 11 + 11 = 51
51 − 30 = 21
Explanation.ExampleResult: The result is the 21st lunar day, waning moon phase.
Explanation.YearRuleText1: A solar year lasts 365 days, while a lunar cycle lasts about 29 and a half days.
Explanation.YearRuleText2: For this reason, the epact increases by about 11 each year, with corrections when it exceeds 30.
Explanation.Note: This method follows a traditional count and does not represent the Moon’s exact astronomical position.
